events.extended_summary: Golborne Road in north Kensington, London, ranks second in the world's coolest streets list, while York Road in Kings Heath, Birmingham, also features. Song Wat Road in Bangkok tops the annual ranking, followed by Fernández de Enciso in Buenos Aires, Vaasankatu in Helsinki and Neil Road in Singapore. Golborne Road, beneath Trellick Tower and associated with Little Morocco, was praised for mixing long-established businesses with newer arrivals, including Portuguese, Moroccan and Middle Eastern cafés, independent retailers and vintage stores like Lisboa Patisserie, Maramia Cafe, Rejina Pyo's boutique and Rellik. York Road was recognized for pub tables spilling across the pedestrianised street, colourful shop fronts and community feel, with the Grade II-listed Hare & Hounds pub dating to 1820 and serving pints since 1907. The list was compiled from nominations by local editors and experts, judged on food, shopping, nightlife, community spirit, street life and independent businesses.
events.micro_summary: Two UK streets named among world's coolest in annual ranking with Golborne Road second.
events.summary: Golborne Road in London ranks second and York Road in Birmingham features in the annual list of world's coolest streets, topped by Song Wat Road in Bangkok, with Fernández de Enciso in Buenos Aires third.

events.extended_summary: Amazon released Melania, a two-part documentary series about First Lady Melania Trump, which consists largely of leftover footage from a theatrical film released 10 months prior. The original movie, directed by Brett Ratner and funded by Amazon, cost $75 million to license and market, $40 million for rights and $35 million for marketing, but earned only $16 million globally at the box office. The new series, totaling 71 minutes, shares the same B-roll footage as the film and focuses on the initial days following the second inauguration. Both projects attempt to position Melania Trump as a lifestyle tastemaker, featuring scenes of her discussing seating plans, boarding Air Force One, and working in her Palm Beach office. However, the series contains no new revelations, instead presenting platitudes and aesthetically pleasing shots without substantive content.
events.micro_summary: Melania Trump's two-part Amazon documentary series reuses footage from a $75 million theatrical flop that earned $16 million.
events.summary: Amazon released Melania, a two-part documentary series about First Lady Melania Trump reusing footage from a theatrical film released 10 months ago. The original cost $75 million and earned $16 million globally, while the 71-minute series offers no new information.

events.extended_summary: President Donald Trump, 80, appeared to fall asleep during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, on November 19. Livestream footage captured the president with his eyes closed for at least 10 seconds while Chinese President Xi Jinping spoke about free and open trade, contrasting with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney who was taking notes. The White House denied the accusations, with Communications Director Steven Cheung calling the claims 'Fake News' and stating Trump was looking at papers, while previous explanations suggested he was merely 'blinking.' Critics mocked the incident as embarrassing, with various commentators sharing the video and joking that the world was safer or laughing at him. A comedy program later released a parody supercut highlighting Trump's history of dozing off during important events, including the 9/11 memorial and NBA finals, joking about a 'Trumpy Nappy White Noise Machine' featuring sounds that lull him to sleep.
events.micro_summary: President Trump appeared to fall asleep for 10 seconds during the APEC summit in China.
events.summary: President Trump, 80, appeared to fall asleep for at least 10 seconds while Chinese President Xi Jinping spoke at the APEC summit in China, prompting mockery from critics and a denial from the White House claiming he was reading papers.

events.extended_summary: Mexican military forces arrested alleged drug lord Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza-Flores, leader of the Sinaloa-based Los Mazatlecos cartel, in Guasave, Sinaloa, on Friday. The operation, conducted by elite forces using stealth and surprise with US intelligence, also captured the group's second-in-command Germán "N" and financial operator José "N". Meza-Flores, listed among the FBI's 10 most wanted fugitives with a $5 million reward, faces US extradition requests for drug trafficking including fentanyl and cocaine. The arrest sparked violent clashes, with militants attacking authorities with gunfire and explosives, setting up roadblocks, and helicopters firing on positions, causing baseball fans to flee. All three detainees were flown to Mexico City for prosecution.
events.micro_summary: Mexican military arrested alleged drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, an FBI top 10 fugitive, in Sinaloa on Friday.
events.summary: Mexican military forces arrested alleged drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, listed among the FBI's 10 most wanted fugitives, and two associates in Guasave, Sinaloa, on Friday, sparking gunfire and roadblocks; he was flown to Mexico City.

events.extended_summary: The COP31 climate summit has gone into overtime as nearly 200 countries remain deadlocked over a draft deal that no longer mentions fossil fuels. The two-week talks in Antalya, Turkiye, were due to end on Friday, when a late closing session approved some technical matters, but not the wider political deal. “We are close to the finish line, but we are not there yet,” COP31 President and Turkiye’s Environment Minister Murat Kurum told delegates. Environmental groups tracking the two-week conference said the meeting lacked ambition to address the ‌worsening climate crisis and was on track to be the “worst COP ever”. A third draft is expected on Saturday, the AFP news agency reported. An opening draft from cohost and lead negotiator Australia on Monday called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels. events.micro_summary: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock.
events.summary: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock. The COP31 climate summit has gone into overtime as nearly 200 countries remain deadlocked over a draft deal that no longer mentions fossil fuels.

events.extended_summary: Hackers breached the US Department of Agriculture and the FBI in separate cyberattacks. The USDA confirmed that a system facilitating payments to farmers was targeted, with concerns that hackers could use it as a backdoor to access sensitive biological research. The FBI is investigating an intrusion into the National Crime Information Center, its second hack since September. The NCIC maintains a nationwide criminal database linking federal, state and local law enforcement, used daily to identify fugitives, check warrants and conduct background checks. Officials expressed concern that hackers could compromise the accuracy of information officers rely on for public safety. It remains unclear whether the breaches are related or who is responsible. The incidents occurred amid a spate of tech outages affecting key American institutions, though officials stated the outages were not linked to criminal activity.
events.micro_summary: Hackers breached the USDA farmer-payment system and the FBI's National Crime Information Center.
events.summary: Hackers breached the US Department of Agriculture's farmer-payment system and the FBI's National Crime Information Center, the second FBI hack since September, raising concerns about compromised law enforcement data and sensitive biological research.

events.extended_summary: Sean Cairncross (left) was appointed by the Trump administration The top cyber-security official in the US government is leaving his post after a little over a year in the job. White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired after losing the confidence of the White House chief of staff, Stephen Miller, according CBS, the BBC's US news partner. Asked about his removal on Friday, President Donald Trump said it was because he was not "good enough". His firing comes after a string of tech outages which hit banking, air traffic control and other sectors. US officials said the outages were not caused by cyberattacks but the blackouts had sparked scrutiny from members of Congress who demanded a clearer explanation of what went wrong. There has been no official confirmation of the removal of Cairncross but Secretary of State Marco Rubio posted on X, external to say Department of Defense
events.micro_summary: White House cyber director ousted after US hit by wave of tech outages.
events.summary: White House cyber director ousted after US hit by wave of tech outages.

events.extended_summary: Kimi Antonelli set the fastest time in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, beating Max Verstappen by 0.258 seconds, but a five-place grid penalty for exceeding his internal combustion engine allocation means the new Formula 1 world champion will start sixth. Verstappen therefore takes pole position, with Mercedes teammate George Russell starting alongside him on the front row after finishing 0.331 seconds behind Antonelli. McLaren's Lando Norris will start third. The penalty was applied despite Antonelli's qualifying performance, which came after he only just crossed the line to begin his final flying lap and was helped by a slipstream from the Racing Bulls. Verstappen and Russell made contact during final practice on Saturday, but neither driver was penalized; Verstappen received only a warning for driving erratically. The race begins at 4am UK time on Sunday.
events.micro_summary: Kimi Antonelli fastest in Las Vegas qualifying but five-place penalty drops him to sixth.
events.summary: Kimi Antonelli was fastest in Las Vegas Grand Prix qualifying but a five-place grid penalty means Max Verstappen starts on pole with George Russell second, while Antonelli drops to sixth.

events.extended_summary: The College Football Playoff rankings have been updated ahead of Week 12, with UCLA and Utah remaining as the only undefeated squads. Notable upcoming matchups include No. 4 UCLA versus Michigan, LSU versus No. 9 Tennessee, No. 14 Ohio State versus Nebraska, top-ranked Georgia versus No. 21 South Carolina, No. 2 Utah versus TCU, and No. 6 Notre Dame versus SMU. No. 8 Indiana is favored by 7.5 points against Washington, backed by the nation's No. 4 scoring defense and quarterback Grant Wilson's 305 passing yards in his first start against USC. No. 5 Texas is favored by 20.5 points against Arkansas after winning four straight games including three against top 25 opponents, while Arkansas is 0-3 against the spread following wins this season.
events.micro_summary: College Football Playoff rankings updated for Week 12 with UCLA and Utah remaining undefeated among top teams.

events.extended_summary: Russian forces launched a triple-tap strike on the Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih on Friday night, killing a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old paramedic while injuring nearly 60 others. Ballistic missiles hit a restaurant parking lot in the city center on World Children's Day, followed by drone strikes targeting rescue workers and a subsequent attack on the same location. Among the wounded, 28 remain hospitalized including children such as a three-year-old girl, with five in intensive care. The attacks damaged 23 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools, businesses, and vehicles, while disrupting water, gas, and electricity supplies across several districts. The strikes occurred in the hometown of President Volodymyr Zelensky, who described the area as an ordinary civilian zone with no military facilities nearby.
events.micro_summary: Russian strikes on Kryvyi Rih killed a 7-year-old boy and a paramedic, injuring nearly 60 others.
events.summary: Russian ballistic missiles and drones struck Kryvyi Rih on Friday night, killing a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old paramedic and injuring nearly 60 others, including rescue workers, in a triple-tap attack on a restaurant parking lot in the city center.

events.extended_summary: Jonathan Rinderknecht, a 30-year-old former ride-share driver, was convicted by a federal jury of starting the Palisades fire in Los Angeles on January 1, 2025. The blaze burned undetected for six days before erupting on January 7, killing 12 people and destroying nearly 7,000 homes across almost 40 square miles in the wealthy Pacific Palisades neighborhood, with damages estimated at $150 billion. Rinderknecht was found guilty on two federal charges of destruction of property by means of fire and arson after a previous trial ended in a mistrial. Prosecutors argued he acted out of anger and resentment toward the wealthy, citing digital evidence placing him at the fire's origin. He faces a mandatory minimum of five years and a maximum of 20 years on each count, with sentencing scheduled for March 17.
events.micro_summary: Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, was found guilty of starting the Palisades fire that killed 12 people.
events.summary: Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, was convicted of arson for starting the January 2025 Palisades fire that killed 12 people and destroyed nearly 7,000 homes in Los Angeles, causing about $150 billion in damage.

events.extended_summary: Investigators uncovered the remains of approximately 170 dead pets dumped across 15 sites in the suburbs of Bulacan near Manila, including dogs and cats found in plastic bags, septic tanks, rivers, and vacant lots. The animals, including Belgian Malinois, golden retrievers, pugs, and puppies, were allegedly sent to Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium in Bacoor, Cavite, for cremation but were discarded instead. The National Bureau of Investigation found no traces of animal remains in ashes given to owners, with forensic tests showing urns contained silicon, iron, potassium, and aluminum. At least 250 pet owners filed complaints, and the Bacoor City government ordered the crematorium closed. Four people are under investigation, and the case has been submitted to the Department of Justice for preliminary investigation under estafa.
events.micro_summary: Pet crematorium dumped 170 dead animals in Bulacan and gave owners fake ashes, prompting 250 complaints.
events.summary: Authorities found remains of about 170 dead pets dumped in Bulacan suburbs near Manila after a crematorium allegedly failed to cremate them. At least 250 owners filed complaints; the business was closed and four people are under investigation for estafa.

events.extended_summary: A necropsy on Fiona, the popular hippo at Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Garden in the United States, showed that the hat she swallowed was lodged deep inside her body and veterinary staff were unable to reach it before she died. The hat was “25 feet [7.60 metres] beyond the final stomach compartment and 50 feet [15.2 metres] from the end of her intestines,” said a statement released on Friday by the zoo in Ohio. Fiona was nine years old when she died. Hippos typically live 40 to 50 years in zoos. The hat she ingested had accidentally been flung into her enclosure. Since her death, fans have covered the zoo with flowers and notes, while others left behind her favourite treats, including melons and pumpkins. “We have received so much love from our community and beyond,” said Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike. The Nile hippopotamus was born prematurely in January
events.micro_summary: Removal of hat inside Fiona the hippo was 'impossible', Cincinnati Zoo says.
events.summary: Removal of hat inside Fiona the hippo was 'impossible', Cincinnati Zoo says. On Thursday, Fiona, a beloved hippo, died after eating a hat that had fallen into her enclosure at the Cincinnati zoo.

events.extended_summary: Ramayana: Part 1, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, and Sai Pallavi and directed by Nitesh Tiwari, has crossed Rs 902.31 crore in India net collections by Day 17, becoming the fourth Indian film to enter the Rs 900 crore club after Baahubali 2, Pushpa 2: The Rule, and Dhurandhar 2. Released on Diwali, the film collected Rs 564 crore in its first week and over Rs 200 crore in its second week, making it the second Hindi film of 2026 to achieve the latter milestone. Daily collections included Rs 75 crore on Day 11, Rs 19.35 crore on Day 15, and Rs 16.30 crore on Day 16, with Rs 22.81 crore earned by evening on Day 17. The worldwide gross reached Rs 1,574.60 crore by Day 16, while the Hindi version became the only Indian-language film to cross Rs 650 crore net.
events.micro_summary: Ramayana: Part 1 crosses Rs 902.31 crore India net collection on Day 17.
events.summary: Ramayana: Part 1 starring Ranbir Kapoor and Yash has crossed Rs 902.31 crore in India net collections on Day 17, becoming the fourth Indian film to reach the Rs 900 crore milestone.

events.extended_summary: The youth wing of India's opposition Congress party staged protests outside Meta offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram on Friday, demanding restoration of Instagram accounts belonging to its leaders. Protesters entered the Hyderabad building, clashed with police, spray-painted slogans in Mumbai, and held banners in Gurugram. The party alleged Meta withheld the accounts on November 19 on orders from the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party. Two accounts were restored after the protests, but thousands of accounts of journalists, creators and influencers critical of the government remain restricted. The youth wing issued a seven-day ultimatum demanding Meta lift restrictions on opposition voices and explain how many accounts were withheld on government orders in the past six months. Police registered a complaint against four leaders in Mumbai and detained some protesters. A BJP spokesperson accused protesters of vandalism. Meta has not issued a statement, though disclosures show it restricted over 5.4 million posts or accounts in India under local laws in the first half of 2026.
events.micro_summary: Indian Youth Congress protests at Meta offices in three cities demand restoration of blocked Instagram accounts.
events.summary: Indian Youth Congress staged protests at Meta offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram demanding restoration of blocked Instagram accounts, with two accounts restored after clashes but thousands of critical accounts still restricted.

events.extended_summary: US President Donald Trump on Friday cited India's 7 per cent GDP growth to criticize the US Federal Reserve for maintaining high interest rates, arguing the American economy could expand 15 to 20 per cent if borrowing costs were reduced. Speaking at the White House, Trump accused the Fed of being "very political," alleging it raises rates whenever the US announces strong economic figures rather than lowering them. He noted India achieved 7 per cent growth despite lower rates and argued stronger US performance should allow lower borrowing costs. Trump also questioned why the US should not have the lowest interest rates globally. His remarks come as US inflation remains above the Fed's 2 per cent target, with annual PCE inflation at 3.6 per cent in September and core PCE at 3.1 per cent.
events.micro_summary: US President Donald Trump cited India's 7 per cent GDP growth to criticize the Federal Reserve's high interest rates.
events.summary: US President Donald Trump cited India's 7 per cent GDP growth to criticize the Federal Reserve's high rates, claiming the US economy could grow 15 to 20 per cent if borrowing costs were lowered.

events.extended_summary: Real Madrid president Florentino Perez announced plans for a free streaming platform in India starting from the 2027 season, offering top UEFA club competition matches without subscription fees. Developed with UEFA and European Football Clubs through their joint venture UC3, India will be the first market for this model. The platform aims to strengthen direct engagement between European clubs and Indian supporters in a country of nearly 1.5 billion people with a young demographic. Beyond free matches, it will offer exclusive content, personalised communication, and membership programmes allowing clubs to connect directly with fans. Perez cited a 15-year-old Real Madrid fan in Mumbai who currently uses unauthorised websites, noting the platform would let him watch legally in high quality while enabling direct communication between the club and supporter.
events.micro_summary: Real Madrid president Florentino Perez announced a free streaming platform for UEFA matches in India starting 2027.
events.summary: Real Madrid president Florentino Perez announced plans for a free streaming platform in India offering top UEFA club competition matches from the 2027 season, developed with UEFA and European Football Clubs to engage fans directly.

events.extended_summary: The Men's Asia Cup for the Blind final in Dhaka between India and Pakistan ended in controversy after rain prevented play. Pakistan were declared champions based on superior run rate, despite India arguing both teams should be joint winners without a reserve day. India boycotted the trophy presentation. The Cricket Association for the Blind in India questioned a Pakistani umpire's neutrality after a video showed him celebrating with Pakistan players through gestures mimicking fighter jets crashing. CABI stated officials must remain neutral. The dispute escalated after World Blind Cricket Council president Sultan Shah reportedly overruled the technical committee's recommendation for joint winners. CABI secretary Shailendra alleged Pakistan used influence to claim the title without playing the final, noting Pakistan had beaten India by one wicket in the group stage while India entered as defending champions from 2016.
events.micro_summary: Rain-hit Asia Cup for the Blind final ends with Pakistan declared champions over India amid umpire neutrality controversy.
events.summary: Pakistan declared Asia Cup for the Blind champions over India after rain-hit Dhaka final decided by run rate despite India's joint winners plea, as CABI questioned a Pakistani umpire's neutrality over a celebratory video.

events.extended_summary: India reached 486-4 at the close of play on day three of the first Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve, taking a 118-run lead with two days remaining. KL Rahul scored 136 off 290 balls, his 13th Test century and first in New Zealand, while Shubman Gill made 98 before being bowled by Jacob Duffy three balls before stumps. Rishabh Pant remained unbeaten on 55 and Anshul Kamboj on 0. Earlier, Yashasvi Jaiswal scored 85 and Devdutt Padikkal 80, making India's top five all score fifty-plus. Jacob Duffy finished with 1-180 from 29 overs, the fourth most expensive figures in New Zealand Test history, while Kyle Jamieson took 1-57. Rahul survived an lbw shout on 5, and Gill successfully reviewed a dismissal on 67. India resumed at 159-1, chasing down New Zealand's first innings total.
events.micro_summary: India reached 486-4 with a 118-run lead after KL Rahul's 136 and Shubman Gill's 98 against New Zealand.
events.summary: India reached 486-4 at stumps on day three of the first Test against New Zealand, taking a 118-run lead as KL Rahul scored 136, Shubman Gill 98, and Rishabh Pant 55 not out.

events.extended_summary: India A and Pakistan A will clash in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 Group B match at West End Park International Cricket Stadium in Doha on Sunday, November 22. Both teams enter the contest with winning starts. India A, led by Tilak Varma, defeated Nepal by 306 runs, scoring 332/9 before bowling out Nepal for 26 in 11.3 overs. Kumar Kushagra (117) and Tilak (107) scored centuries, while Prince Yadav and Harshit Rana took five and four wickets. Pakistan A, captained by Abdul Samad, beat UAE by 61 runs, posting 245 and dismissing UAE for 184. Shamyl Hussain (62) and Maaz Sadaqat (53) top-scored, with Sufyan Moqim and Ali Raza taking three wickets each. Pakistan defeated India A by 128 runs in the 2023 final. India A play UAE on November 24.
events.micro_summary: India A face Pakistan A in Doha after 306-run and 61-run opening victories in Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026.
events.summary: India A will face Pakistan A in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 in Doha on Sunday after both teams won their opening matches by 306 runs and 61 runs respectively.

events.extended_summary: India's campaign at the Hong Kong Open Super 500 concluded on Saturday with both remaining players suffering straight-game defeats in the semifinals. The sixth-ranked men's doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty lost 18-21, 19-21 to Malaysia's eighth-seeded Man Wei Chong and Tee Kai Wun despite holding a 4-1 head-to-head advantage. Lakshya Sen, seeking a third consecutive title after wins at the Hylo Open and Kumamoto Masters Japan, was beaten 21-13, 21-13 by Denmark's Anders Antonsen. The defeats left India without a finalist in the tournament. Satwik and Chirag, who had won titles in Singapore and China earlier this year, started strongly but could not maintain their lead against the Malaysians in a closely contested match featuring sharp exchanges and powerful smashes.
events.micro_summary: Satwik-Chirag lost 18-21, 19-21 and Lakshya Sen 21-13, 21-13 in Hong Kong Open semifinals.
events.summary: India's campaign at the Hong Kong Open Super 500 ended Saturday as Satwiksairaj Rankireddy-Chirag Shetty lost 18-21, 19-21 to Malaysia's Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun and Lakshya Sen fell 21-13, 21-13 to Denmark's Anders Antonsen in semifinals.

events.extended_summary: A 40-year-old woman named Sunita was killed while her 20-year-old son Dhruv and 20-year-old daughter-in-law Niti sustained burn injuries after a fire broke out in a residential building in west Delhi's Raghubir Nagar on Saturday. The fire started among domestic articles on the first floor of the building. All three sustained burn injuries and were rushed to Guru Gobind Singh Hospital in a CATS ambulance. Dhruv suffered 20 per cent burns while Niti suffered 60 per cent burns. Sunita was declared dead by doctors while Dhruv and Niti are undergoing treatment. The Delhi Fire Services received a call about the blaze at 12.05 pm and rushed multiple fire tenders to the spot. The fire was brought under control by 12.25 pm.
events.micro_summary: A 40-year-old woman died and two relatives suffered burns in a west Delhi fire on Saturday.
events.summary: A 40-year-old woman was killed and her son and daughter-in-law sustained 20% and 60% burns respectively after a fire broke out in a residential building in west Delhi's Raghubir Nagar on Saturday.

events.extended_summary: Eeramalla Sai Teja, a 25-year-old native of Telangana's Nalgonda district, died in a multi-vehicle collision on Interstate 90 near Canajoharie, New York, on November 18 at 6:34 pm. The crash occurred when his vehicle struck a deer and became disabled in a traffic lane, then was hit by a cargo van, triggering a chain reaction involving two other vehicles. Sai Teja sustained severe injuries and was declared dead at St Mary's Hospital. A passenger in his car was airlifted to Albany Medical Center in critical condition, and a cargo van passenger was also injured. He had moved to the US for higher studies, lived in Utica, and secured a job one week before the accident. He is survived by parents Eeramalla Prasad and Srikanya. Eastbound lanes between exits 29 and 28 were closed until 1:15 am on November 19. Police are investigating and arranging repatriation of his remains to India.
events.micro_summary: Eeramalla Sai Teja, 25, died in a New York multi-vehicle crash on November 18 after hitting a deer.
events.summary: A 25-year-old man from Telangana died in a chain-reaction crash on Interstate 90 in New York on November 18 after his car hit a deer and was struck by a cargo van; he had secured a job one week prior.
